name: Lou Malnati's Pizzeria
description: Chicago's legendary deep-dish pizza since 1971. The Malnati Chicago Classic with its butter crust is a must-try.

name: Portillo's
description: Classic Chicago-style hot dogs, Italian beef, and chocolate cake shake. A Chicago institution.

name: The Violet Hour
description: Award-winning craft cocktail bar in Wicker Park. No sign on the door—look for the mural.

name: Intelligentsia Coffee
description: Pioneering third-wave coffee roaster. The Millennium Park location is perfect for people-watching.

name: Girl & The Goat
description: Stephanie Izard's acclaimed restaurant with bold, globally inspired small plates.

name: Big Star
description: Honky-tonk taqueria in Wicker Park with excellent tacos and a killer whiskey selection.

name: Garrett Popcorn
description: Iconic Chicago popcorn shop. The Chicago Mix (caramel and cheese) is legendary.

name: Millennium Park
description: Chicago's crown jewel park featuring Cloud Gate (The Bean), Crown Fountain, and free summer concerts.

name: Chicago Riverwalk
description: 1.25-mile pedestrian waterfront along the Chicago River with restaurants, kayak rentals, and city views.

name: Lincoln Park Zoo
description: One of the oldest free zoos in the US. Located in the heart of Lincoln Park with lakefront views.

name: Lakefront Trail
description: 18.5-mile paved path along Lake Michigan. Perfect for biking, running, and rollerblading.

name: Montrose Beach
description: Popular beach with a dog-friendly area, volleyball courts, and stunning skyline views.
address: 4400 N Lake Shore Dr, Chicago, IL 60640

name: Garfield Park Conservatory
description: One of the largest conservatories in the US. Free admission with stunning indoor gardens year-round.
address: 300 N Central Park Ave, Chicago, IL 60624

name: Metro Chicago
description: Legendary indie music venue in Wrigleyville. Intimate setting for up-and-coming and established acts.

name: The Second City
description: World-famous improv comedy theater. Alumni include Tina Fey, Steve Carell, and Bill Murray.

name: Kingston Mines
description: Chicago's premier blues club. Two stages, live music every night, no cover weeknights.

name: Art Institute of Chicago
description: World-class art museum housing iconic works including A Sunday on La Grande Jatte and American Gothic.

name: Hideout Inn
description: Tiny, eclectic bar hidden in an industrial area. Live music, comedy, reading series, and community events.

name: Thalia Hall
description: Historic Pilsen venue hosting concerts, dance parties, and cultural events in a stunning 1892 building.

name: Randolph Street Market
description: Monthly indoor/outdoor market featuring vintage, antiques, fashion, and artisan goods.

name: Wicker Park Vintage Shops
description: Cluster of vintage and thrift stores along Milwaukee Ave. Great for unique finds and retro fashion.

name: Open Books
description: Nonprofit bookstore where all proceeds fund literacy programs. Two locations with great used book selection.

name: Pilsen Murals
description: Outdoor gallery of vibrant street art and murals throughout the Pilsen neighborhood celebrating Mexican-American culture.

name: Chicago Architecture Center
description: Interactive exhibits on Chicago's architecture plus boat tours on the Chicago River.

name: Greater Chicago Food Depository
description: Chicago's food bank. Volunteer to sort and pack food for families in need across Cook County.
address: 4100 W Ann Lurie Pl, Chicago, IL 60632

name: Lincoln Park Community Services
description: Serve meals, organize donations, or help with after-school programs in the Lincoln Park community.

name: Chicago Cares
description: Volunteer hub connecting individuals to service projects across Chicago. One-time and recurring opportunities.

name: Navy Pier
description: Chicago's lakefront landmark with a Ferris wheel, restaurants, shops, and seasonal events.

name: Skydeck Chicago (Willis Tower)
description: 103rd-floor observation deck with The Ledge glass balconies extending over the street below.

name: Superdawg Drive-In
description: Iconic drive-in hot dog stand since 1948. Look for the giant hot dog figures on the roof.

name: Revival Food Hall
description: Downtown food hall with 15+ chef-driven stalls, craft cocktails, and a curated beer list.

name: Promontory Point
description: Scenic lakefront park in Hyde Park with panoramic skyline views. Popular for picnics and sunsets.
address: 5491 S DuSable Lake Shore Dr, Chicago, IL 60615

name: Museum of Science and Industry
description: One of the largest science museums in the world. Highlights include a captured U-505 submarine and coal mine tour.
address: 5700 S DuSable Lake Shore Dr, Chicago, IL 60637

name: Logan Square Farmers Market
description: Beloved Sunday farmers market with local produce, prepared foods, and live music.

name: Wrigley Building
description: Iconic 1920s white terra-cotta tower on the Magnificent Mile. Glows beautifully when illuminated at night.

name: Tribune Tower
description: Neo-Gothic landmark on Michigan Ave with fragments of famous buildings from around the world embedded in its walls.

name: Marina City
description: Iconic 'corn cob' twin towers designed by Bertrand Goldberg. A Chicago architectural landmark since 1964.

name: Field Museum of Natural History
description: World-class natural history museum home to SUE, the largest T. rex ever discovered.
address: 1400 S DuSable Lake Shore Dr, Chicago, IL 60605

name: Shedd Aquarium
description: One of the world's largest indoor aquariums with 32,000+ animals including beluga whales and dolphins.
address: 1200 S DuSable Lake Shore Dr, Chicago, IL 60605

name: Adler Planetarium
description: America's first planetarium. Stunning skyline views from the tip of the Museum Campus peninsula.
address: 1300 S DuSable Lake Shore Dr, Chicago, IL 60605

name: Soldier Field
description: Historic stadium home of the Chicago Bears. The neoclassical colonnades are a must-see landmark.

name: 12th Street Beach
description: Hidden urban beach just south of Adler Planetarium with great skyline views and fewer crowds.
address: 1200 S Linn White Dr, Chicago, IL 60605

name: Chess Records / Willie Dixon's Blues Heaven
description: Legendary recording studio where Muddy Waters, Chuck Berry, and the Rolling Stones recorded. Now a blues museum.

name: Buddy Guy's Legends
description: Blues club owned by living legend Buddy Guy. Live blues every night in a storied South Loop venue.

name: Jazz Showcase
description: Chicago's oldest jazz club, running since 1947. World-class jazz performances in an intimate setting.

name: Green Mill Cocktail Lounge
description: Historic jazz club and former Al Capone speakeasy. Live jazz and the famous Uptown Poetry Slam.

name: Chicago Pedway
description: Underground pedestrian walkway system spanning 40 blocks beneath the Loop. A hidden city beneath the city.
address: Millennium Station, 151 E Randolph St, Chicago, IL 60601

name: Lurie Garden
description: 5-acre botanical garden hidden at the south end of Millennium Park. A secret prairie oasis in the city.

name: The Dearborn
description: Upscale American tavern in the Loop with a speakeasy atmosphere and seasonal craft cocktails.

name: Graceland Cemetery
description: Victorian-era cemetery and open-air architectural museum. Final resting place of many famous Chicagoans.

name: Oz Park
description: Lincoln Park neighborhood park with Wizard of Oz character statues. A nod to L. Frank Baum's time in Chicago.
